gemma-4-26b-a4b.prompt_summary: Very fast 3.8B-active QAT multimodal synthesizer for writing, visual analysis, extraction, and medium-complexity planning; choose it when Gemma quality matters but dense 31B latency does not.
strengths: Preserves Gemma's prose and visual strengths with very fast low-active-parameter QAT inference.
Good quality-throughput compromise for general multimodal assistance.
limitations: Does not automatically replace a coding specialist or the dense 31B quality lane.
Configured vision still depends on the packaged projector and deployment verification.
prompting: Give explicit acceptance criteria for synthesis or planning; speculative decoding changes speed, not model behavior.

evidence.notes: Architecture and family behavior are publisher-backed; practical role and speed guidance reflects product and operator judgment.

gemma-4-e2b.prompt_summary: Tiny, very fast QAT generalist for tightly scoped rewriting, extraction, classification, captions, and light image understanding; use a larger model for reasoning, coding, or research authority.
strengths: Very fast, low-cost QAT first pass for simple language and visual tasks.
Gemma-style prose is often more natural than similarly small utility models.
limitations: Limited depth, coding reliability, and multi-step tool persistence.
Native audio capability is not exposed by the current llama.cpp package.
prompting: Give one explicit task, the output shape, and a short example; do not rely on hidden planning.

evidence.notes: Capability facts are publisher-backed; role fit is a conservative product inference pending broader local use.

gemma-4-e4b.prompt_summary: Fast compact QAT assistant for short-form writing, translation, summarization, and document or image extraction; more coherent than E2B but still not an unattended agent or large-code model.
strengths: Very fast QAT route with a useful balance of readable prose and multimodal extraction.
Good intermediate choice when E2B is too shallow and 12B is unnecessary.
limitations: Not dependable for long tool chains, deep planning, or final technical judgment.
Native audio and video are not exposed by the current llama.cpp package.
prompting: Use direct natural-language instructions and specify the desired concision and deliverable.

evidence.notes: Hard capabilities are official; relative writing and role guidance combine operator experience with family-level inference.

gemma-4-12b.prompt_summary: Fast one-card QAT writer and visual analyst; prefer it for polished prose, editing, image recognition, and document synthesis when maximum coding or agentic ability is not required.
strengths: Produces polished, natural prose and follows tone or audience instructions well.
Strong practical image recognition and document inspection for its deployment size.
The official QAT-derived deployment is notably fast for its quality tier.
limitations: Less reliable than coding-focused models on long autonomous implementation and tool loops.
Native audio and video are not exposed by the current llama.cpp package.
prompting: State the audience and tone, and name the visual evidence or document details that must be inspected.

evidence.notes: Native and configured capabilities are publisher-backed; the writing, image, and speed guidance reflects recurring owner experience.

gemma-4-31b.prompt_summary: Careful editor and high-quality visual or general analyst; prefer it for nuanced writing, critique, summarization, and image understanding when latency is secondary.
strengths: Strongest Gemma lane for polished prose, careful interpretation, and visual analysis.
Good at separating evidence, observations, and conclusions when asked explicitly.
limitations: Dense execution is slower than the 26B-A4B lane and throughput-oriented MoE alternatives.
It should not be selected solely by size for autonomous coding or tool orchestration.
prompting: Specify audience and tone, and ask it to separate direct observations from conclusions.

evidence.notes: Official family results support the quality tier; prose and image preference is reinforced by recurring operator experience.

qwen-3.5-9b.prompt_summary: Compact multimodal worker for small coding tasks, extraction, translation, visual questions, and routine reasoning; use a larger model for architecture, broad orchestration, or research authority.
strengths: Strong coding, structured-output, and multimodal utility for a small deployment.
Useful as a focused worker that can be run more cheaply or in parallel.
limitations: Not a dependable final strategist for complex systems or long autonomous workflows.
Its prose is generally more utilitarian than the comparable Gemma writing lanes.
prompting: Enable thinking for difficult work and use non-thinking mode for routine transformations; provide an exact output contract.

evidence.notes: Capabilities and publisher results are official; role boundaries partly extrapolate from Qwen family behavior.

qwen-3.6-35b-a3b.prompt_summary: Fast implementation and tool-execution worker for coding, code search, structured tools, and parallel subagents; give final planning or architectural judgment to a stronger supervisor.
strengths: Low active parameter count makes it a high-throughput coding and tool worker.
Publisher guidance and practical use favor concrete repository tasks and explicit tests.
limitations: Can look capable early in a nested workflow and still lose the larger orchestration thread.
The current PreFer artifact omits its native visual projector and is configured text-only.
prompting: Use the exact Qwen tool format, define acceptance tests, and keep the objective concrete and bounded.

evidence.notes: Coding and tool surfaces are official; the worker-versus-orchestrator distinction is reinforced by operator and agent-harness experience.

qwen-3.8-27b.prompt_summary: High-intelligence dense coder and generalist for repository work, debugging, tools, research synthesis, difficult reasoning, and bounded planning; its template defaults to xhigh reasoning, so choose a lower mode only when the task or latency goal calls for it.
strengths: Strong practical coding, tool use, synthesis, and controllable reasoning in a one-card quality lane.
Dense execution favors quality and consistency over the 35B-A3B route's throughput.
limitations: Xhigh reasoning can carry substantial token and latency costs, but difficult planning, proofs, or architecture work may benefit materially.
Image input depends on the packaged F16 projector and still requires deployment-specific visual validation.
prompting: Disable thinking for work that should not reason. With thinking enabled, use only low, medium, or xhigh: low asks for brief focused thinking, medium adds no effort instruction, and xhigh is the careful-validation default.
On the pinned b11058 runtime, pass reasoning control through the template kwargs path and verify it is rendered; do not assume an OpenAI-style top-level reasoning_effort field is forwarded.

evidence.notes: Capabilities and supported reasoning values come from the released model and template; role guidance is qualitative product judgment reinforced by operator experience.

ornith-1.5-9b.prompt_summary: Economical coding and tool subagent for narrow, executable objectives such as patching, repository navigation, and parallel implementation; do not use it as the final architect or research authority.
strengths: Publisher tuning targets terminal coding agents and self-improving tool workflows.
Small enough to use as an inexpensive focused worker with a packaged image projector.
limitations: Independent validation is still thin, especially for visual behavior and long agent loops.
Not intended to own final architectural or high-stakes conclusions.
prompting: Preserve the model's modified chat and think/tool format, lower temperature for precise coding, and give one executable objective.

evidence.notes: The publisher model card and harness support the coding role; independent route and behavior validation remains limited.

ornith-1.5-35b-a3b.prompt_summary: Persistent, fast agentic coder for bounded multi-file implementation, repository or browser agents, and structured tool loops; validate it before trusting prose, visual judgment, or final architecture.
strengths: Low active compute supports persistent, multi-step implementation at useful throughput.
Publisher training and harness focus directly on coding agents and tool use.
limitations: Publisher quality claims should not be assumed to transfer unchanged to PreFer's llama.cpp route.
The configured projector and long tool loops still need route-specific validation.
prompting: Use the exact bundled template and parser, pin the artifact, and provide bounded tools with explicit acceptance tests.

evidence.notes: Publisher documentation targets agentic coding; local artifact, parser, and visual stability remain verification items.

nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b.prompt_summary: Throughput-first text worker for bulk summarization, extraction, classification, rewriting, and routing; select a quality-focused model for final adjudication or difficult reasoning.
strengths: Three active billion parameters and speculative decoding make it attractive for high-throughput text work.
Configurable thinking permits a speed-versus-quality choice without changing models.
limitations: It is a throughput role, not the strongest intelligence point in the current roster.
Hybrid state, long-context, and tool behavior remain more runtime-sensitive than ordinary dense text models.
prompting: Keep routine jobs bounded and non-thinking; enable thinking only when the added latency is justified by task difficulty.

evidence.notes: Architecture, context, and throughput positioning are publisher-backed; exact local tool behavior remains a verification item.

muse-glimmer-30b.prompt_summary: Eager visual and tool agent for screenshots, OCR, documents, visual workflows, and schema-driven actions; give it strict tool boundaries and stopping rules rather than unrestricted autonomy.
strengths: Purpose-built for local multimodal agents, with publisher-documented visual and agentic training targets.
Controllable reasoning strength and failure-recovery training suit bounded interactive workflows.
limitations: Operator reports indicate that tool use can become over-eager or inconsistent without clear boundaries.
It is not the natural first choice for prose-only work when Gemma is available.
prompting: Set `Reasoning strength` explicitly, limit the tool budget, require confirmation for irreversible actions, and define a stop condition.

evidence.notes: Architecture, modalities, quant quality, and intended roles are publisher-documented; tool eagerness comes from early operator reports.

glm-4.7-flash.prompt_summary: Fast one-card reasoning and coding helper for bounded implementation, search, tools, drafting, and synthesis; use GLM-5.2 or another supervisor for the hardest long-horizon work.
strengths: Its three-billion-active MoE architecture makes it a fast coding, browsing, and agent worker for its total size.
Useful qualitative quality-throughput balance for a single 96 GB deployment.
limitations: Not the preferred final authority when larger high-intelligence routes are available.
Agent behavior depends on preserving its thinking and tool-template semantics.
prompting: Use the exact GLM template and tool schema; preserve thinking across multi-turn agent tasks and define a bounded completion condition.

evidence.notes: Architecture and intended capabilities are publisher-backed; precise PreFer role and speed judgment still needs route-level experience.

deepseek-v4-flash-preview.prompt_summary: Deliberate text planner retained for compatibility, long-context synthesis, and regression comparisons; route new high-end work to the 0731 successor when its client protocol is supported.
strengths: Known compatibility route with strong reasoning and unusually affordable long context for its size.
Useful as the stable comparison point for newer DeepSeek V4 releases.
limitations: It is the Preview lineage rather than the current preferred successor.
The preserved route is target-only and lacks the newer DSpark acceleration path.
prompting: Use the exact Preview chat protocol, allow adequate reasoning space, and keep tool turns consistent with its preserved template.

evidence.notes: The route has direct operational history; its present role is primarily compatibility and regression comparison.

deepseek-v4-flash-0731.prompt_summary: High-end text planner and research supervisor for complex plans, coding design, long synthesis, and tool orchestration; hand routine implementation to faster workers and preserve its version-specific protocol.
strengths: Strong release-specific agent and coding evidence with very long native context.
DSpark can materially improve decode speed on the configured two-GPU quality route.
limitations: Large artifacts and a specialized encoding or tool protocol make it a poor generic drop-in.
It is expensive for routine work and should supervise rather than absorb every implementation task.
prompting: Use the versioned response and tool format, preserve reasoning content across tool turns, and state the desired reasoning mode and completion boundary.

evidence.notes: Protocol and model capabilities are official; quality and DSpark gains remain workload- and runtime-dependent.

glm-5.2.prompt_summary: High-end text supervisor for difficult reasoning, research synthesis, coding design, and long-context planning; reserve it for high-leverage work rather than cheap fan-out.
strengths: Flagship long-horizon model with flexible thinking effort and a publisher-supported one-million-token context.
Good supervisor candidate for complex plans, evidence synthesis, and coding architecture.
limitations: Its multi-accelerator footprint and latency make it wasteful for routine worker tasks.
The local GGUF route still needs contract, tool, and long-context validation on target hardware.
prompting: Provide the objective, evidence requirements, decision criteria, and sufficient reasoning budget; keep the exact GLM template.

evidence.notes: Flagship capabilities are publisher-backed; local quality, speed, and route behavior remain deployment-specific.

glm-5.2-reap.prompt_summary: Fit-optimized GLM-5.2 derivative for constrained high-end planning and reasoning; prefer the full model for rare knowledge or quality-critical authority unless this exact derivative has been compared.
strengths: Expert pruning opens a materially smaller multi-GPU deployment while retaining the GLM-5.2 interface.
Useful when the full 753B route is operationally unavailable.
limitations: Behavioral equivalence to full GLM-5.2 is not established and the model card reports a higher loop rate.
The current GGUF uses a compatibility workaround for shared sparse-attention indexer tensors.
prompting: Use the base GLM template, pin the exact derivative, and require explicit evidence checks for quality-critical conclusions.

evidence.notes: Artifact and pruning facts are documented; practical behavioral equivalence remains a verification item.

smollm2-135m.prompt_summary: Tiny text helper for health checks, simple labels, formatting, and toy completions only; never treat it as a reasoning, coding, research, tool, or writing model.
strengths: Starts quickly and cheaply enough to validate basic serving and request plumbing.
limitations: Its tiny capacity is unsuitable for meaningful assistant quality or contract-rich tool use.
prompting: Give one short task, a strict output shape, one example, low temperature, and a short output limit.

evidence.notes: Model size and text capability are official; the smoke-test-only role is an explicit PreFer product decision.
